session.task: Implement ADR-0001: resilient, idempotent outbound calls for the checkout flow

events.reason: Following ADR-0001. The ordering constraint is load-bearing: idempotency must be applied before the retry loop, or retries turn the manual double-charge into an automatic one. Building a single transport rather than per-client retries so the policy lives in one seam.
events.notes: Scope per ADR-0001: resilience.py + both clients + main.py

events.reason: Create demo/resilience.py. Order of application: derive an idempotency key from the logical operation (order_id) and short-circuit an already-succeeded key; then a bounded retry loop (max 3, base 100ms, full jitter, transient failures only); all behind a per-dependency circuit breaker keyed by base URL. sleep/rng are injected so backoff is deterministic in tests.

Route StripeClient.charge through the transport with order_id as the idempotency key. This closes the double-charge bug: a retried charge reuses the key and dedupes instead of creating a second charge.
Route GitHubClient.create_receipt_issue through the same transport so the receipt write gets the same backoff + breaker. Keyed on the GitHub base URL so a GitHub outage trips independently of Stripe.
Wire main.py's /checkout to the updated clients. Orchestration is unchanged — the reliability policy now lives entirely in resilience.py, so main.py stays thin.

Tests pass, including deterministic cases for backoff timing, idempotent-retry dedupe (no double charge), and circuit-breaker-open. Distributed breaker state deferred to ADR-0002 per the review's human override.
